transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in today?

Well… I guess it’s little mistakes piling up. I’ll write the wrong time on a senior-center class sheet, or measure a board and still cut it just a bit short because I missed some small print. Things like that.

When you miss these small details—like fine print or measurement marks—do you notice it's specifically hard to see things up close, or does it feel more like you're just not paying attention or forgetting?

I don’t think it’s my eyes, exactly. I can see it if I slow down. It’s more like I just skip over the little part—like the fine print on a measurement or the time on a sheet—and then I don’t catch it until after.

Have you noticed this kind of missing-small-details pattern your whole life, even back in school or early adulthood, or is this something that's really only started or gotten noticeably worse recently?
Yeah… it goes back a ways. Even in grade school, teachers would say I was smart enough, but I’d forget my books, lose homework, or just be looking out the window unless somebody kept me on task.
Do you notice these attention slips happening in more than one area of your life—like at work, at home, and in social situations—or is it mostly limited to just one setting?

It’s… more than one place, I guess. Not just one setting. I’ve backed off helping lead a couple of the DIY workshops because of the mix-ups, and at home my wife ends up checking plans so I don’t mess up family visits or things at the center.
Besides these attention slips, have you noticed things like feeling restless, having trouble sitting still, interrupting others, or acting on impulse without thinking it through?

A little, yeah. Mostly I just get kind of… restless if I have to sit through a whole meeting, or even a quiet evening at the condo. I start wanting to get up and check on something or just putter around.
Thinking back to your childhood or teenage years, did you notice that same restlessness or urge to get up and move around, or was that something that only started later in adulthood?

I think it was there some, but I notice it more now. Like sitting through a whole meeting, or even just a quiet evening at the condo, I get that ants-in-my-pants feeling and want to get up and check something or putter around.
Would you say these attention slips and restlessness have caused real problems—like conflicts, missed responsibilities, or safety issues—or are they more of an annoyance that you work around?

It’s more than just annoying, I guess. I’ve had to step back from helping lead a couple of the DIY workshops because of mix-ups, and my wife kind of double-checks plans now so I don’t throw off family visits or things at the center.
Do you often find yourself interrupting conversations, blurting things out before someone finishes speaking, or having trouble waiting your turn in line or in discussions?
Not really… I mean, maybe once in a while I’ll start talking a little too soon, but I don’t think that’s a big thing for me. Waiting in line doesn’t bother me much.
Have you been feeling unusually anxious, low in mood, or not sleeping well lately that might be contributing to these concentration and restlessness issues?

I don’t know… I wouldn’t say unusually. I have my normal worries, I guess, but nothing that feels like the main reason. Sleep’s not perfect every night, but I haven’t really noticed a big change there.
